title: Smallness of objects in a Grothendieck category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ its *size* $|M|$ is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of $M$. Let $M$ be an object of $\mathcal A$ and $\alpha$ an ordinal whose cofinality is greater than $|M|$. Then $M$ is $\alpha$-small with respect to monomorphisms: for every system $(B_\beta)_{\beta<\alpha}$ in $\mathcal A$ indexed by $\alpha$ whose transition maps $B_\beta\to B_{\beta'}$ ($\beta\le\beta'<\alpha$) are monomorphisms, every morphism $M\to\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\alpha}B_\beta$ factors through $B_\beta\to\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\alpha}B_\beta$ for some $\beta<\alpha$.

proof.text: Write the colimit of the monomorphism chain as the union B = colim_{\beta<\alpha} B_\beta, viewing each B_\beta as a subobject of B. For a morphism f:M\to B, the inverse images M_\beta=f^{-1}(B_\beta) form an increasing family of subobjects of M, and AB5 gives colim_{\beta<\alpha} M_\beta = f^{-1}(colim_{\beta<\alpha}B_\beta)=M.

There are at most |M| distinct subobjects among the M_\beta, because |M| is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of M. Choose a set S of indices of cardinality at most |M| that contains an index for every distinct M_\beta. Since cof(\alpha)>|M|, S has an upper bound \widetilde{\alpha}<\alpha. Monotonicity then gives M_\beta\subseteq M_{\widetilde{\alpha}} for every \beta, so the union equality in the preceding step forces M_{\widetilde{\alpha}}=M.

proof.text: The equality M_{\widetilde{\alpha}}=M means that f(M) is contained in B_{\widetilde{\alpha}}. Because B_{\widetilde{\alpha}}\hookrightarrow B is monic, f factors through the structure map B_{\widetilde{\alpha}}\to colim_{\beta<\alpha}B_\beta. Thus M is \alpha-small with respect to monomorphisms.
